hypothesis: Multisampling alone was rejected because it moved the horizon skyline band of water_reflection far from the supersampled reference — 77 percent of the guard loss sat in one percent of the blocks, all at rows 336 to 352, five to sixteen times too bright. A partially covered pixel still shades once, at the pixel centre, and that centre can lie outside the triangle, so every varying is extrapolated. On a 1.5 km facade an extrapolated surface_uv lands on a different window cell, and a lit window is orders of magnitude brighter than the wall beside it. Interpolating at the centroid of the covered samples keeps the shading point inside the primitive.

provenance.origin: V2-3i, after the first MSAA candidate was rejected by the detail guard
provenance.disproved: A nearest-of-four depth resolve was measured first and changed the water_reflection block distance by 0.0001 at both scales, so the depth resolve is not the cause.
provenance.note: centroid is only distinguishable from the default when a pixel is partially covered, which cannot happen without multisampling, so at one sample this changes nothing. The qualifier has to match on both sides of the stage boundary.
